prompt: Audit a £50m UK compliance software market claim and test whether £4m entrant revenue is credible.
input: Fictional training data. Decision: £6m UK entry investment; market-size gate £20m year-three supplier recurring revenue and entrant target £4m/year. Customer: regulated firms with 100-999 employees; excludes services. Low/base/high drivers: eligible firms 7000/7500/8000; workflow fit 60/70/75%; paid adoption 45/60/70%; seats 11/14/16 per adopter; realized annual seat price £650/720/780. Independent CURRENT supplier scan: 4 providers at £5m each and 8 at £1.2m. No current-to-year-three growth or bundled-revenue bridge is provided. Entrant can win 80 customers/year for three years, before churn. Audit the £50m claim, calculate scenarios, reconcile limitations and test reachability.
rubric: Defines scope, metric, period, and units
Uses an independent cross-check and reconciles differences
critical_guardrails: Do not manufacture a narrower range or period reconciliation
Do not declare the £4m target reachable without a capacity path
output:
# Compliance software sizing — current-session response

## Decision

Do not approve the full £6m entry investment on this evidence. The fictional year-three model gives a £31.752m base and a £13.5135–52.416m range. £50m is an upside result, not a defensible base. The base clears the £20m gate; the low case fails. The entrant's £4m target is not supported by the stated sales capacity.

## Definition and calculations

Metric: annual supplier recurring revenue in year three, UK regulated firms with 100–999 employees, excluding services. Units are firms × workflow-fit share × adoption share × seats/firm × pounds/seat/year = pounds/year.

Low: 7,000 × .60 × .45 × 11 × £650 = £13,513,500/year.
Base: 7,500 × .70 × .60 × 14 × £720 = £31,752,000/year.
High: 8,000 × .75 × .70 × 16 × £780 = £52,416,000/year.

The supply-side scan gives 4 × £5m + 8 × £1.2m = £29.6m current annual revenue. It is independent of the buyer/seat model, but not period-aligned. The base is 7.27% higher; this difference is not evidence of a growth rate. Missing bundled-revenue and period bridges prevent reconciliation or a narrower forecast range. All inputs are fictional assumptions, not verified market facts.

## Reachability and next gate

At £720 × 14 = £10,080 annual revenue/customer, £4m requires ceil(4,000,000/10,080) = 397 active customers. The plan supports 80 × 3 = 240 before churn, or £2.4192m/year, leaving a 157-customer gap. This is an upper bound absent churn, ramp and sales-cycle data.

At the other base inputs, the £20m market gate needs paid adoption of 20m/(7,500 × .70 × 14 × £720) = 37.79%. That one-driver threshold does not make the joint downside safe. Strategy should validate adoption/seats with buyer evidence, quantify the supply-side scope/time bridge, and show an owned channel-capacity plan before investment approval. Neither uncertainty robustness nor obtainable revenue is demonstrated.
